reasoning: Both outputs are factually accurate. A is a clean, readable snapshot, but it mostly describes and catalogs what is on the pages. It gives no evidence IDs and does not separate what was seen from what was inferred. Its 10 patterns are claims with no conditions for when they apply. B traces every claim to evidence IDs, tags each one as observed, inferred or hypothesis, and gives each cross-site pattern a shared rule, how each site differs, and when the pattern transfers. It explains the reasoning behind the differences (for example, Stripe works as a portal with many entry points while Notion is a single funnel), lists combinations to avoid with reasons, and audits which patterns have weak evidence on one side. B is long and dense, but it matches the user's research goals much better.
a_strengths: Concise, scannable section-order and design-language tables
Specific, accurate hex colors, font sizes and page lengths
Practical guidance on what to borrow, including one warning about mixing styles
Short limitations section (A/B experiments, colors auto-extracted, mobile only checked at first screen)
a_weaknesses: No evidence IDs, so claims cannot be traced
Does not separate observed from inferred; interpretive claims such as 'drawn characters make AI feel friendly' are stated as fact
Patterns have no rules for when they apply and little reasoning about why they work
Leans toward a feature inventory and UI description
b_strengths: Each claim is tagged as observed, inferred or hypothesis and cites screenshot or source evidence IDs
Cross-site patterns have a shared rule, the per-site difference and conditions for transfer
Design-language table includes the trade-off behind each difference
Self-audit marks the weaker evidence (motion, Notion marquee, Stripe responsive screenshots split across A/B experiment groups) as hypotheses
Explains which combinations to avoid and why
b_weaknesses: Very long (about 65KB across reports and observations), with heavy ID jargon that slows a designer down
Observations log lists a tablet screenshot that is not in the folder
XP-07 says sites 'don't remove blocks', yet Notion's mobile drops the hero product image (noted, but the rule is loosely worded)
